items.title: Which cannot?
Explaining XOR
items.prompt:
A friend who knows no maths beyond Stage 0 asks why “one neuron can't do XOR”. Write the explanation you would give.

(a) Say what a neuron and XOR are, in plain words. (b) Draw the four corners in words (say where each sits and which fire) and say what one neuron does to that picture. (c) Give the short argument that no weights and bias work, with a reason for each step. (d) Say how two layers fix it, naming the three neurons.
items.model:
**(a)** A neuron adds up its inputs, each times a weight, adds a bias, and says yes (1) if the total is above 0, else no (0). XOR says yes when exactly one of two inputs is 1.

**(b)** Picture a square: (0, 0) bottom left, (1, 0) bottom right, (0, 1) top left, (1, 1) top right. XOR says yes at the top left and bottom right, no at the other two corners. A neuron's yes and no are split by one straight line, where its total is 0. The yes corners sit on one diagonal and the no corners on the other, and no straight line puts the two diagonals on different sides.

**(c)** Suppose weights $w_1$, $w_2$ and bias $b$ worked.

1. (0, 0) must say no, so $b \le 0$.
2. (1, 0) and (0, 1) must say yes, so $w_1 + b > 0$ and $w_2 + b > 0$.
3. Two true “greater than” statements can be added: $w_1 + w_2 + 2b > 0$.
4. Take $b$ from both sides: $w_1 + w_2 + b > -b$, and $-b \ge 0$ by step 1, so $w_1 + w_2 + b > 0$.
5. That is the total at (1, 1), so it says yes. XOR needs no. So no weights and bias work, whatever their size.

**(d)** Use two layers. First, an OR neuron (2, 2, −1) and a NAND neuron (−2, −2, 3). Then an AND neuron (2, 2, −3) takes their two outputs. OR and NAND are both yes only at (0, 1) and (1, 0), so AND gives XOR. Each first-layer neuron draws one line, and two lines fence off the diagonal.

rubric.text: Defines a neuron (weighted sum, bias, fires above 0) and XOR in plain words
Describes the four corners, which fire, and that one neuron splits them with one straight line
Gives the argument: b ≤ 0, the two single-input inequalities added, and the conclusion that (1, 1) fires
Notes the argument holds for any weights, however large
Builds XOR from two layers (OR and NAND feeding AND) and checks it
